journey.title: Tab away after typing an unavailable delivery date
journey.goal: Leaving the date field with Tab closes the calendar even when the typed date is outside the delivery window

steps.title: Type a date outside the delivery window

functionalJourney.title: Move the delivery into June with the pointer
functionalJourney.goal: Clicking through the calendar to June and choosing a day fills the delivery date

guards.title: Type a valid delivery date and Tab away
guards.goal: A correctly typed date is committed and the calendar closes when the user tabs away

plan.root_cause: The datepicker's keydown handler only hides the calendar when the entered date is considered valid; when the date is outside the allowed min/max range, the handler does not trigger hide, leaving the picker open when focus leaves via Tab.
plan.repair_strategy: Add a blur event listener to the input field that calls the datepicker's hide method, ensuring the calendar closes whenever the input loses focus regardless of date validity.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Keyboard users can navigate away from the date field using Tab and the datepicker will close, preventing focus trap and preserving logical tab order.
functional_risks: Possible unintended hiding if other code expects the datepicker to remain open after blur (e.g., manual interaction after blur). However hide() is a no-op for inline pickers and safe to call multiple times, so risk is low.
verification_requirements: Typing a valid date (within min/max) and pressing Tab closes the datepicker and moves focus to the next field.
Typing an invalid date (outside min/max) and pressing Tab closes the datepicker and moves focus to the next field.
Clicking outside the input field closes the datepicker.
Selecting a date via the calendar grid still behaves as configured (e.g., autohide).

plan.root_cause: The datepicker's keydown handler only hides the calendar when the entered date is valid (within min/max range). When the date is invalid, pressing Tab does not trigger hide, leaving the picker open. The existing blur listener should close the picker but does not fire reliably in this scenario.
plan.repair_strategy: Add a capture-phase keydown listener on the input field that hides the picker on Tab regardless of date validity, ensuring the calendar closes when the user tabs away.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Keyboard users can navigate away from the date field using Tab and the datepicker will close, preventing focus trap and preserving logical tab order even when the typed date is outside the allowed range.
functional_risks: Minimal risk: the new listener runs in capture phase and hides the picker before the existing keydown handler. The existing handler may also hide for valid dates, but hide() is idempotent.
verification_requirements: Typing a valid date (within min/max) and pressing Tab closes the datepicker and moves focus to the next field.
Typing an invalid date (outside min/max) and pressing Tab closes the datepicker and moves focus to the next field.
Clicking outside the input field closes the datepicker.
Selecting a date via the calendar grid still behaves as configured (e.g., autohide).
